Subject: SOC2 Type II + bridge letter request for FinServCare renewal

Hi Diego / Marissa,

We are preparing for FinServCare's annual vendor review and need Redwood's SOC2 Type II report for the period covering 2026-01-01 to 2026-10-31. In addition, the procurement team has asked whether you can provide a bridge letter covering the three-month gap from your last report to the current date.

A couple of finserv-specific asks:
- Confirmation of which cloud provider controls we rely on (compute, storage, KMS, logging).
- A list of subprocessors that handle customer data for FinServCare (names + contract date).
- If any cloud provider SOC reports are used as a carve-out (subservice organization), please confirm the scope and whether you have a vendor bridge/attestation.

Can you confirm what you can share and an estimated timeline? We need an initial packet for the security committee by 2026-12-09.

Thanks,
Sam Keller
Vendor Risk Manager — FinServCare
sam.keller@finservco.com
+1 415-555-0198

Sam — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to support. High-level plan below and a couple of clarifying Qs.

What we will provide (initial deliverables):
- Redwood SOC 2 Type II (most recent report) — redacted PDF summary + control index (see attached summary stub).
- A draft bridge letter that covers critical control assertion continuity for the gap period (we can draft and route for signature).
- Subprocessor register (names, roles, onboarding dates) and a CSV index of third-party SOC reports we rely on (we will mark which are treated as subservice carve-outs).

Clarifying questions so we scope correctly:
1) When you say "carve-out" do you require vendor-level carve-out mapping tied to each control (i.e., which control elements are satisfied by CloudVendor SOC reports vs Redwood's controls)?
2) Do you require copies of the underlying cloud provider SOC reports or is a mapping + CloudVendor-provided bridge letter sufficient?
3) Any specific evidence artifacts you need (example: retention policy excerpts, egress logs, KMS custody statements)?

Internal owners: Marissa will coordinate the SOC artifacts; Kim will pull the subprocessor list and cloud-report index.

Target timeline: initial packet to you by 2026-12-08; bridge draft by 2026-12-09 pending legal sign-off. If you need faster turnaround, please flag which items are highest priority.

Diego Fernandez
Head of Trust & Security — Redwood Inference

- Control mapping table: column for Redwood control, column for evidence artifact, column for third-party dependency (if any), and column "covered by cloud provider SOC? (Y/N)".

From: Olivia Tran <olivia.tran@audits.cloudvendor.com>

Cc: Sam Keller <sam.keller@finservco.com>
Date: 2026-12-04 08:17 PST
Subject: Re: SOC2 Type II + bridge letter request for FinServCare renewal

Hi all — Olivia from CloudVendor audits here. I was looped in to clarify how our SOC coverage is typically treated for customers doing vendor assessments. A few points: 

1) Our SOC 2 report covers the control categories for Compute (virtual machines), Block Storage, Object Storage, and our Key Management Service (KMS) for the audited region (us-west-2) during the report period.
2) We do NOT cover application-layer controls or customer-managed encryption keys (if customers import and manage keys in their own KMS). Those are generally considered customer responsibilities.
3) We can provide a standard bridge letter at customer request that confirms no material control changes since the report end date for the specified services — however, bridge letters are scoped to services and date ranges; we need Redwood to specify which CloudVendor services Redwood treats as subservice organizations for FinServCare.

Deliverables we can provide on short notice:
- CloudVendor SOC 2 report copy (redacted) via secure link.
- Service-level bridge letter template for requested services + date range.

To proceed, can you provide:
- A named list of CloudVendor service IDs used in FinServCare's configuration (e.g., cv.compute-std, cv.object-store, cv-kms-usw2).
- A short statement of whether Redwood or FinServCare manages encryption keys for the data in scope.

Happy to coordinate a quick 30-min sync if that's easier.

Best,
Olivia Tran
Senior Audit Liaison — CloudVendor Audits
olivia.tran@audits.cloudvendor.com

Please find attached an evidence checklist we will use for FinServCare (Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_Summary.pdf) and a stub CSV for CloudVendor mapping (CloudVendor_SOC_Report_Index.csv). I'll also send a DocuSign envelope for the non-disclosure addendum + bridge-letter request should you confirm.
